references.title: LAX's SkyLink People Mover Could Open to Passengers on January 6
Troubled LAX People Mover delayed again — and it might not be the last time (Los Angeles Times)
More delays: LAX train contractor buys more time for testing (LAist)
LAX People Mover to Open in January (MyNewsLA.com)

changes.after: LAX's SkyLink Now Aims to Carry Passengers From January 6, Past Its December 8 Deadline
changes.before: LAX's SkyLink Reaches Its December 8 Deadline to Carry Passengers

changes.after: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, had to enter passenger service by its 8 December 2026 longstop date; contractor LINXS now says service could begin on 6 January 2027, with "no assurances" it will not slip again.
changes.before: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, must enter passenger service by its project longstop date of 8 December 2026 or its developer LINXS risks a technical default on $1.2 billion of bonds.

changes.after:
• In a 16 September disclosure filing, LINXS said it will need time beyond the 8 December completion deadline; if all goes well the train could be running by 6 January 2027, though "there can be no assurances" the date will not slip further
  • Before opening, the train must pass 30 consecutive days of testing, an independent review and an assessment by Los Angeles World Airports, and a utility agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power must be completed
  • Recent testing was paused twice to fix track components that "accommodate movement resulting from temperature changes, seismic activity and normal structural behavior"
  • Bondholders agreed to push the lender longstop date on the SkyLink bonds back to December, lining it up with the construction longstop and averting a technical default that would have been triggered in October
  • Fitch's Seth Lehman said the best case is a 30-day commissioning test starting by the end of September, a utility agreement and public service beginning by December 8, "but it's very tight"; a delay beyond December would need LAWA's consent
  • The project is more than 99% complete, and a dispute over the interconnection agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, which LAX has not signed, remains; the developer has money for debt service only into early to mid-2027
  • The California Municipal Finance Authority issued $1.2 billion of bonds for LINXS in 2018; Fitch cut them to BB in July 2026 after LINXS sued the city on July 9
  • Construction was first due in March 2023; systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, and the project longstop date is December 8, 2026
  • An August 2026 report had the $3.34 billion system targeting passenger service in October 2026

Notable features

  • A 2.25-mile driverless train with six stations linking the terminals, the LAX/Metro Transit Center and the Rental Car Center
